key_insight: The paper introduces a standardized benchmarking framework that lets researchers evaluate and compare neuromorphic controllers on soft robotic platforms, enabling reproducible, hardware-aware assessments of embodied intelligence.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of standardized, reproducible benchmarks for neuromorphic controllers in soft robotics—fragmented evaluation protocols, inconsistent metrics (energy, latency, robustness), and poor comparability across simulators and hardware.
method: Define task suite and metrics tailored to embodied neuromorphic agents (e.g., energy use, latency, control robustness, adaptability).
Provide an integrated pipeline combining simulation and real-world hardware interfaces for soft robots and neuromorphic processors.
Deliver an open-source evaluation suite and reference controllers to enable reproducible experiments and fair comparisons.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners a practical way to measure controller performance across energy, speed, and robustness trade-offs, accelerating reproducible research and informed co-design of neuromorphic algorithms and soft bodies.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing simulation-to-hardware flow: tasks → neuromorphic controller → soft robot → metrics collection.
Radar/comparison chart of key metrics (energy, latency, robustness, adaptability) across controllers/hardware.
Schematic illustration of a soft robot with an embedded neuromorphic chip (annotated sensors, actuators, and data flows).
Leaderboard or heatmap visualizing benchmark results across methods and devices for quick comparison.
paper_title: A benchmarking framework for embodied neuromorphic agents
paper_authors: Giulia D’Angelo, Jens E. Pedersen, Taimoor Hassan, Matteo Cianchetti, Josh Bongard
